frequency_question: How often do programmed operational scale-ups execute their mandatory sequential steps and reach target volume milestones within a designated 112-day window once initiated?
membership_rule: Includes any formally announced institutional debt management or open market operation volume expansion program where a new per-operation purchase ceiling is established and tested; excludes ad-hoc emergency interventions without pre-announced procedural ramp-up schedules.

cases.name: Federal Reserve QE2 Treasury purchase acceleration (2010)
Federal Reserve maturity extension program (Twist) scaling (2011)
Federal Reserve QT taper and adjustment phase (2019)
Bank of England gilt purchase emergency scale-up (2022)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named instances representing major institutional liquidity and debt management scaling operations; universe is small due to rarity of specific $4B+ scale-up thresholds.
known_gaps: Relatively small sample size of exact fiscal buyback scale-ups specifically, supplemented by broader central bank open market operation volume adjustments.
skeleton: Central bank debt management operation adjustment cycles since 2008 involving volume target changes, categorized by procedural review phases (announcement, dealer consultation, initial test operation, full volume execution).
multiplier: 4 historical benchmark scale-up cycles, all successfully completing procedural execution phases within 3 to 4 months.
validity_reason: Institutional operational mechanics and primary dealer auction/settlement timelines change slowly over decades.
